system.name: LifeLine
system.one_liner: an object-page lifetime alignment garbage collector that minimizes memory copying for mobile devices

content.subject: how ZCGC picks between zero-copy page remapping and object copying for each page based on its survival ratio

elements.name: User space
elements.role: swim-lane label for the region holding to-space and from-space pages

elements.name: Kernel space
elements.role: swim-lane label for the region where the movement decision and its execution happen

elements.name: To space
elements.role: destination memory region that migrated/compacted pages are moved into

elements.name: Access
elements.role: annotates the arrow showing the mutator accessing a to-space page during migration

elements.name: From space
elements.role: source memory region holding pages awaiting migration, split by survival ratio

elements.name: Low ratio
elements.role: from-space pages with a low live-object survival ratio

elements.name: High ratio
elements.role: from-space pages with a high live-object survival ratio

elements.name: Scheme planner
elements.role: estimates each page's survival ratio from marking-phase statistics and feeds the decision

elements.name: Check page survival ratio
elements.role: decision point that routes a page to a movement strategy based on its survival ratio

elements.name: Object Copying
elements.role: strategy for sparse/medium-density pages: copy only the surviving objects

elements.name: Page Remapping
elements.role: strategy for dense pages: remap the whole page via userfaultfd without copying data

elements.name: Per-page survival ratio
elements.role: y-axis of the accompanying curve, the metric the decision is based on

elements.name: Threshold
elements.role: marks the configurable survival-ratio cutoff that separates the two strategies

elements.name: Turning point
elements.role: marks the knee where the survival-ratio curve drops sharply, motivating where the threshold sits

relations.what: from-space pages (low/high ratio) are read by the kernel-space decision
supplies each page's estimated survival ratio to the decision
high survival ratio (dense page) routes to remapping
low/medium survival ratio (sparse page) routes to copying
remapped pages become to-space pages via page-table updates only
copied survivor objects are written into to-space
the threshold is set near the curve's turning point, where remapping and copying costs cross

decisions.question: is the page's survival ratio above the high threshold (dense) or below it (sparse)?
branches: high ratio -> Page Remapping (zero-copy page-table update)
low/medium ratio -> Object Copying (copy only surviving objects)

content.key_idea: A single per-page survival-ratio threshold, set at the point where the cost curves of remapping and copying cross, is enough to route each page to whichever of the two movement strategies is cheaper.
content.reading_order: top-down through User space (From space's Low/High ratio pages) into Kernel space's decision diamond, which fans out left to Object Copying and Page Remapping and back up into To space; the curve on the right explains where the threshold sits

evidence: a movement planner cooperates with the OS to decide, on a per-page basis
The thresholds correspond to the turning point in Figure 12, where the costs of remapping and copying intersect

summary: Figure 12 explains LifeLine's near-zero-copy garbage collector (ZCGC), which decides per page whether to remap or copy during compaction. From-space pages are grouped by their live-object survival ratio: pages with a high ratio are dense and go to Page Remapping, which uses userfaultfd to retarget page-table entries into to-space without touching the data; pages with a low or medium ratio are sparse and go to Object Copying, which copies only the surviving objects. A Scheme planner supplies each page's estimated survival ratio, reused from the GC's marking pass, to a central decision diamond that routes pages to whichever strategy applies. The accompanying curve plots per-page survival ratio against time and marks a Turning point where the curve drops sharply, motivating where the remap/copy Threshold is set.
